memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The pig is also unclean; although it has a divided hoof, it does not chew the cud. You are not to eat their meat or touch their carcasses. Of all the creatures living in the water, you may eat any that has fins and scales. But anything that does not have fins and scales you may not eat; for you it is unclean. - Deut 14:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The food laws continue, marking out which creatures of land and water were clean or unclean for Israel. To us these distinctions can seem strange or arbitrary, but for Israel they served a clear purpose: with every meal, God's people were reminded that they belonged to Him and were called to live differently from the nations around them. The dinner table became a daily lesson in identity and belonging.

There is something worth noticing here about how God shaped His people. He did not leave their sense of belonging to occasional grand ceremonies; He wove it into the fabric of daily life. Every time an Israelite chose what to eat, they were reminded of who they were and to whom they belonged. Belonging to God was not an abstract idea but a lived, everyday reality.

As we've seen, these particular laws are not binding on believers today — in Christ we are free, and no food is unclean in itself. But the principle that our belonging to God shapes daily life remains true and precious. As Christians, we carry a new kind of daily reminder: we belong to Christ, purchased by His blood, and that identity shapes how we live in the ordinary moments. Paul writes, "You are not your own; you were bought at a price. Therefore honor God with your bodies" (1 Cor 6:19-20). Our belonging to God is meant to touch our everyday choices, marking us out as His. Let the truth that you belong to Christ shape how you live today, not just in worship, but in the ordinary rhythms of your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I live daily with an awareness that I belong to Christ?
- How might my belonging to God shape my ordinary choices?
- What "daily reminders" help me remember whose I am?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I belong to You, purchased at a price by the blood of Christ. Help me live each day aware of whose I am, letting that identity shape my ordinary choices. May my whole life honor You, in worship and in the everyday. Amen.
